harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 as a persistent Prometheus server monitoring node2, node3, and node4. All named targets are UP with current host metrics. Prometheus listens only on 127.0.0.1:9090, while each node_exporter accepts port 9100 traffic only from node1. Configuration and access controls survived serial restarts of all four nodes.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled Prometheus on node1.
Configured named targets node2:9100, node3:9100, and node4:9100.
Bound Prometheus exclusively to 127.0.0.1:9090 and disabled node_exporter on node1.
Installed node_exporter on node2–node4 and bound it to each node's managed IPv4 address.
Added persistent nftables restrictions allowing exporter collection only from node1.
Verified allowed collection from node1 and rejected access from other nodes.
Restarted node1–node4 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Named targets and current host metrics are queryable on node1
evidence.summary: The final valid configuration contains node2:9100, node3:9100, and node4:9100; all targets report UP and return current node_uname_info series.

evidence.requirement: Prometheus interface remains local to node1 on port 9090
evidence.summary: Prometheus is ready with its sole listener at 127.0.0.1:9090, and access through node1's managed IP is rejected.

evidence.requirement: Each node_exporter endpoint is limited to collection by node1
evidence.summary: node1 directly collected metrics from every exporter. After restarts, each exporter and its source-filtering nftables service recovered; representative non-node1 connections to all three exporters were rejected.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 92ec88af-041e-4dc3-b2b9-800263b2b2cb; restart was acknowledged; boot ID changed to d0c0761b-11c9-4a4e-8c23-588fcfb22d66; exporter, firewall, listener, direct metrics, and Prometheus UP state recovered.
